The old Exit-intent modal becomes one of four ways a popup can open, and your existing message, coupon and reporting history move across automatically. Worth taking on its own merit if you ever want to tell customers you are closed, run a seasonal message, or hand out a code — and worth it regardless if you used exit intent, because that modal could never appear on a phone.
upgrade_notice.11.0.5: Recommended for every shop charging a cash-on-delivery surcharge. The block checkout decides that surcharge before it knows which payment method the customer chose, so orders could be placed without it and card orders could be placed still carrying it. Rooster One now reconciles the surcharge against the payment method the order was really placed with, before the customer is charged, and records the correction in the order notes. Staff-created orders are untouched.
upgrade_notice.11.0.4: Recommended for any shop using the withdrawal right. The link in an order email now opens the order itself: it used to land on a form that already knew the order number but asked for the email address the message had just been sent to, then sent a second email before anything could happen. The link is signed, so the customer sees their items straight away. Also fixes the withdrawal button arriving in English on translated emails, stops the form reappearing after you submit it (which had customers sending the same request two and three times), and renames the second "Reason (optional)" box to "Other comments".
upgrade_notice.11.0.3: Recommended for everyone. The first time you open Rooster One after updating it now explains what you have installed and why it is one plugin rather than twelve, with the free/Pro split stated plainly; a short optional survey sits folded underneath. Every Rooster One screen gains a feedback button and a link to our Viber support group. Also corrects the site-profile badge, which claimed Opportunities, cornerstone pages and demand scores were "all weighted on revenue" — none of the three works that way, and the explanation now describes what each actually uses.
upgrade_notice.10.1: Recommended for every shop selling at a distance in the EU. Adds a complete withdrawal-button implementation for Directive (EU) 2023/2673, which applies with no transition period once your member state has transposed it: a permanent button that works for guests, no reason and no prior contact required, partial withdrawal on multi-item orders, and an acknowledgement email on a durable medium in your shop's own language. Return vouchers now pass through an operator who checks the label before the customer ever sees it, the pickup address is editable, and labels printed at a courier's portal can be uploaded. Ten international courier drivers added — DHL Express, FedEx, UPS, USPS, Royal Mail, DHL Paket, Sendcloud, Colissimo, BRT and Correos Express. The withdrawal feature ships disabled; switch it on once your returns policy and terms are ready. Also fixes a DHL Paket billing number that could be accepted against another account, and courier settings being blanked on save.
upgrade_notice.10.0: Recommended for everyone. Adds a searchable index of every screen in the plugin (Ctrl+K from anywhere), a written description on every page and tab, and a site-profile badge in the header showing whether Rooster One reads your site as a shop, a catalogue or a content site. All source strings are now English with the original wording preserved as translations, so nothing your customers see changes. Also fixes a bug where the AI settings form could still store OpenAI — a provider dropped in May — and corrects a misleading AI-credits message that sent operators to re-check a connector that was already working.
upgrade_notice.9.5: Recommended for everyone, and important if you run on multisite or host several shops on one server. Updating or deactivating no longer drops any database table — a network deactivation previously discarded twelve working tables plus your live sessions and session archive, and two schema migrations could empty the purchase-history rollup or your stored survey responses on update. Report windows such as "this month" now follow the timezone in Settings → General rather than the server clock, so figures no longer shift when your host is in a different timezone from your shop. Also prevents a single marketplace order being imported as two WooCommerce orders. Recommendation caches are cleared once on upgrade, so expect a brief cache-miss on product pages immediately afterwards.
upgrade_notice.9.2: Recommended if your site has ever been restored, migrated or cloned. Database backups omit stored routines by default, which could leave the surveys, web-push, product-needs and session-analytics jobs failing every night with "PROCEDURE … does not exist" — permanently, since reactivating the plugin did not rebuild them. Those jobs now detect and repair their own routines, with no added cost on storefront requests.

upgrade_notice.8.7: Makes more of Rooster One's native blocks (Recommendations, Product Slider, Product Variations Gallery) discoverable in the block editor and on the plugin page, documents the full block library, and clarifies the "Post Related Product Categories" block name. aieo/semantic-related.title: Semantic Related Content
aieo/semantic-related.description: The content the semantic engine relates to this page.

aieo/brand-azindex.name: aieo/brand-azindex
aieo/brand-azindex.title: AIEO Brand A-Z Index
aieo/brand-azindex.description: Server-rendered A-Z brand directory. Every letter A–Z (plus '#' for non-Latin brands) is always present; empty letters render disabled. Sticky letter bar + per-letter brand grid with product counts. Reads exclusively from wp_aieo_core_brand_vitals.

aieo/store-locator.name: aieo/store-locator
aieo/store-locator.title: AIEO Store Locator
aieo/store-locator.description: Grid or list of all your store locations — address, phone, opening hours and Google Maps / review links.

aieo/opening-hours.name: aieo/opening-hours
aieo/opening-hours.title: AIEO Opening Hours
aieo/opening-hours.description: A store location's opening hours. Auto-resolves on a store page, or set a location slug.

aieo/store-map.name: aieo/store-map
aieo/store-map.title: AIEO Store Map
aieo/store-map.description: A single store's location map (keyless Google Maps embed) plus a directions link. Auto-resolves on a store page, or set a location slug.

aieo/business-info.name: aieo/business-info
aieo/business-info.title: AIEO Business Info
aieo/business-info.description: A store location's address, phone, opening hours and Google links — from your Locations & Reviews data.

aieo/google-reviews.name: aieo/google-reviews
aieo/google-reviews.title: AIEO Google Reviews
aieo/google-reviews.description: Live Google reviews pulled from the local cache. Single location, mixed feed, or cards grid.

aieo/store-hero.name: aieo/store-hero
aieo/store-hero.title: AIEO Store Hero
aieo/store-hero.description: Shop-page header hero in the category-hero style (centred image, title, horizontal line). Listing title, heading and description come from the bound location. Auto-resolves on a store page, or set a location slug.

aieo/store-info.name: aieo/store-info
aieo/store-info.title: AIEO Store Info (address, phone, hours)
aieo/store-info.description: Structured store contact info — address, clickable phone, and per-day hours. Reads from post meta + the linked Google location row.

aieo/category-lead.name: aieo/category-lead
aieo/category-lead.title: AIEO Category Lead
aieo/category-lead.description: The current category's description, falling back to its name when it has none. For blog category archive headers.

aieo/blog-hero.name: aieo/blog-hero
aieo/blog-hero.title: AIEO Blog Hero (Latest Post)
aieo/blog-hero.description: Featured latest-post hero with the category-hero look: a top title, the newest post's title as the headline, its excerpt as the description and its featured image — all clickable. On a blog category/tag archive it features that term's latest post.

aieo/category-hero.name: aieo/category-hero
aieo/category-hero.title: AIEO Category Hero
aieo/category-hero.description: The queried category's hero — image, title and description — auto-filled from the term, for product or blog category archive headers.

aieo/blog-subcategories.name: aieo/blog-subcategories
aieo/blog-subcategories.title: AIEO Blog Subcategories (Dropdown)
aieo/blog-subcategories.description: A dropdown of the current blog category's subcategories, styled like the blog-post categories dropdown. Renders nothing when the category has none.

aieo/page-hero.name: aieo/page-hero
aieo/page-hero.title: AIEO Page Hero
aieo/page-hero.description: Manual hero — top title, left headline, right description and desktop/mobile images. Identical look to the category hero, usable on any page.

aieo/category-footer-hero.name: aieo/category-footer-hero
aieo/category-footer-hero.title: AIEO Category Footer Hero
aieo/category-footer-hero.description: The category's SEO footer text beside the category image (image left, rich text right) with the hero divider line. Auto-fills from the queried product category.

aieo/category-chips.name: aieo/category-chips
aieo/category-chips.title: AIEO Category Chips
aieo/category-chips.description: A row of clickable category chips for the current archive — the term's child categories.
